text:
Marta G: Hi team — newbie hiccup. I moved my dev machine over to Colima and now my Postgres container dies on start: "could not open file "postmaster.pid": Permission denied". I have PG data mounted to ~/workspace/app/pgdata. Also my app sometimes gets "ERR NOAUTH" talking to Redis even though I set REDIS_PASSWORD in .env. Any quick ideas?

Omar: welcome! Two common things: 1) Colima host mounts often show up owned by root in the VM; 2) stray/alternate redis instances or env-file mismatches cause NOAUTH. For PG, prefer a named volume, but to keep the host mount you can chown inside Colima to uid 999.

Omar: ```bash
colima ssh
sudo chown -R 999:999 /home/youruser/workspace/app/pgdata
exit
docker compose up -d db
```

Devon: Also check your Postgres image. If you're on alpine/slim it might not have extension packages (eg pgvector) and an init SQL that calls CREATE EXTENSION will fail with "could not open extension control file". Use the repo's dev image or a Debian-based postgres image with the extension installed.

Marta G: I was using postgres:15-alpine. That explains the pgvector error I saw later. For Redis I ran `docker ps` and found an old redis container from a previous experiment — stopped it and auth issues mostly went away.

Omar: Nice. One extra tip: if you map the DB port to the host (ports: - "5432:5432") and you also have a local Postgres (brew), you'll get port conflicts. Use a different host port like 55432:5432 or stop the local service.

Devon: Quick checklist we tell new hires: 1) prefer named volumes for PG; 2) if host bind required, chown inside colima to uid 999; 3) match the dev image (extensions); 4) ensure the correct .env is loaded (`docker compose --env-file .env.dev up`); 5) `docker ps` to spot stray containers.

ops-bot: dev-runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/local-db-setup — see "Colima & host mounts" and "PG image & extensions" :memo:

Marta G: Chowned inside Colima and switched to the repo dev image + named volume. Everything came up fine. Thanks for the tips :thumbsup:
